βαπτιστής.definition: one that dips: baptizer, the Baptist, Ev.Matt.3.1, cf. J.AJ18.5.2, etc.: metaph. of the Passion, Ev.Luc.12.50

βάπτω.definition: trans., dip, . . Od.9.392; Pl.Ti.73e, cf. Emp.100.11; Ar.Ec.216; Arist.HA605a29, de An.435a2:—Pass., iron in process of being tempered, Plu.2.136a; and of coral, become hard, Dsc.5.121

βαρβαρίζω.definition: behave or speak like a barbarian; trans., 'murder', mangle, Luc.Merc.Cond.24

βαρβαρίκιον.definition: name of a foreign garment, POxy.1684.5, 9

βαρβαρισμός.definition: use of a foreign tongue or of one's own tongue amiss, barbarism, Arist.Po.1458a26, Diog.Bab.Stoic.3.214, Ph.1.124, Plu.2.731e; A.D.Synt.198.7

βαρβαρότης.definition: nature or conduct of a Tz.H.9.972, Sch.E.Hec.1129

βαρβαρόφωνος.definition: speaking a foreign tongue; speaking bad Greek, Str.14.2.28

βαρβαρόω.definition: make barbarous: only used in Pass., to become barbarous, E.Or.485, Antipho Soph.Oxy.1364.274; PLond.5.1674.22 ; unintelligible, of birds, S.Ant.1002

βαρβιτιστής.definition: player on the barbiton, name of play by Magnes, Sch.Ar.Eq.519

βαρέω.definition: Aeol. v. infr., fut. Luc.DMort.10.4: pf. D.C.78.17:-Pass., v. infr.:-weigh down, depress, Luc. l. c. ; Procop.Arc.14; Hermog.Inv.2.7; IG14.830.15 , cf. POxy. 1159.2 ; J.BJ2.14.1, cf. D.C. l. c.:-Pass., . . Sapph.Supp.…

βαρυαχής.definition: Dor. for bellowing; awakening sore lament, S.OC1561, Sch

βαρυαχθής.definition: very heavy, Sor.1.55; very burdensome, Nonn.D.40.155

βαρυβρεμέτης.definition: loud-thundering, S.Ant.1117:—also prob. in AP7.394 :—fem. Orph.H.10.25

βαρύβρομος.definition: loud-roaring, Hom.Fr.25; B.16.76; Trag. only in lyr., E.Ph.183, Hel.1305; Id.Hyps.Fr.41.80; loud-sounding, Id.Hel.1351, Ba.156, cf.Ar.Nu.313; Lasus1

βαρύγδουπος.definition: loud-thundering, loud-roaring, Pi.O.8.44; Id.P.4.210, cf. AP9.674; Ion Lyr.9.3

βαρύγλωσσος.definition: grievous of tongue, v.l. for LXXEz.3.5

βαρύγυιος.definition: weighing down the limbs, wearisome, Opp.H.5.63; AP6.190.9

βαρυδαιμονία.definition: grievous ill-luck, Antipho2.2.2; surliness, churlishness, Lys.4.9, Ph.1.487,558

βαρυδαίμων.definition: gen. pressed by a heavy fate, luckless, Alc.37 A., cf. E.Alc.865, Ar.Ec.1102, Cat.Cod.Astr.2.162.30

βαρύζηλος.definition: exceeding jealous or envious, Lyc.57; AP5.242

βαρυηκοέω.definition: to be hard of hearing, Hp.Morb.2.4

βαρυήκοος.definition: hard of hearing, Aret.SD1.4; Act., impairing the hearing, Hp.Aph.3.5, cf. Ph.2.99, S.E.M.6.49

βαρυηχής.definition: deep-voiced, D.S.5.31, cf. Opp.H.4.317; deep-roaring, Orph.Fr.168.28; LXX3 Ma.5.48

βαρυθυμέω.definition: to be weighed down: to be melancholy or indignant, LXXNu.15.16, App.BC2.20; D.S.20.41:—Med., Plu.Sull.6

βαρυθυμία.definition: sullenness, Arist.VV1251a4, Andronic.Rhod.p.570M.; heaviness of heart, depression, J.AJ16.10.5, Plu.Mar.40: pl., Id.2.477e

βαρύθυμος.definition: heavy in spirit: indignant, sullen, E.Med.176, cf. Call.Cer.81, etc.; opp. Plu.2.13e: Sup., Phld.Ir.p.64 W. Adv. Alciphr.2.3; rejected by Poll.3.99

βαρύθω.definition: to be weighed down; abs., to be heavy, AP7.481 ; . . A.R.1.43:—Pass., Max.212, Q.S.13.6

βαρυκαρπέω.definition: bear a heavy crop of fruit, Aegyptus 5.129

βαρυκέφαλος.definition: large- or heavy-headed, of dogs; metaph., top-heavy, Vitr.3.3.5

βαρύκτυπος.definition: heavy-sounding, loud-thundering, epith. of Zeus, h.Cer.3, Hes.Op.79; of Poseidon, Id.Th.818, Pi.O.1.72, Pae.4.41; also of the sea, AP9.753

βαρύλογος.definition: vented in bitter words, Pi.P.2.55; offensive, of certain Stoic tenets, Phld.Sto.Herc.339.12

βαρύμοχθος.definition: toilsome, AP10.97; hard-working, ib.5.469; epith. of Heracles, APl.4.102

βαρύνω.definition: metaph., oppress, weary, Pi.P.1.84; X.Ap.9; of cold, Arist.Somn.Vig.456b26; make more grievous, Ph.2.425:— Pass., to be oppressed, distressed, Simon,184.5, Pi.N.7.43, S.El.820, Th.8.1; by calamities, A.Ag.836, cf. 189…

βαρυόπας.definition: loud-voiced, of Zeus, in acc. Pi.P.6.24

βαρυπενθής.definition: = sq., Ph.2.269, IG12.675.6; causing grievous woe, B.13.12; APl.4.134

βαρύποτμος.definition: = of persons, S.Ph.1096 ; of sufferings, grievous, Id.OC1449 : Comp. Plu2.989e: Sup. Id.TG5, Ph.1.637; but E.Ph.1345

βαρύπους.definition: gen. of a club, heavy at the end, APl.4.104

βαρύπυκνος.definition: in the lower part of the , Aristid.Quint.3.10, Cleonid.Harm.4, etc

βαρυσκελής.definition: heavy in the legs, slow, Trag.Adesp.250

βαρυσκίπων.definition: gen. with a heavy club, Call.Fr.120

βαρύσταθμος.definition: weighing heavy, Ar.Ra.1397, Canthar.2, Arist.EN1142a22; Plu.Lys.17

βαρύστομος.definition: heavy in pronunciation, of the first; of heavy, i.e. abusive, mouth, Nonn.D.48.420

βαρύστονος.definition: groaning heavily; of things, heavily lamented, grievous, S.OT1233, Orac. ap. Paus.10.9.11

βαρυσύμφορος.definition: weighed down by ill-luck, in; Act., calamitous, Them.Or.15.184c

βαρυτιμέω.definition: raise the price of goods, EM759.5, Suid. s.v

βαρύτιμος.definition: punishing severely, of the gods; very costly, Str.17.1.13, Ev.Matt.26.7

βαρύτλητος.definition: Dor. bearing heavy; Pass., ill to bear, B.13.4; APl.4.245

βαρυτονέω.definition: pronounce with the grave accent, D.H.2.58: abs., use the grave accent, Cleonid.Harm.12

βαρυτονητέος.definition: to be marked with the grave accent, Sch.Ar.Ra.864, al

βαρύτονος.definition: deep-sounding, of; Gramm., of enclitics, unaccented, A.D.Pron.35.25; of words, not oxytone, ib.38.12, D.T.674.18, etc. Adv. POxy.1012 Fr. 16.16, Eust.41.3, Moer.109

βαρύφθογγος.definition: loud-roaring, h.Ven.159, B.8.9; deep-lowing, of cows, Arist.GA787a33; loud-twanging bowstring, Pi.I.6.34; deep- toned, AP6.51

βαρυφροσύνη.definition: melancholy, Plu.2.710f , Fr.inc.146; indignation, Id.Cor.21, Porph. ap.Stob.1.49.60

βαρύφρων.definition: gen. heavy of mind; weighty of purpose, grave-minded, Theoc.25.110

βαρυφωνία.definition: Ion. deepness of voice, a bass voice, Hp.Aër.8, Alex.311, Arist.GA786b35

βαρύφωνος.definition: with a deep, bass voice, opp. Hp.Aër.6, Arist.GA786b7, etc

βαρύψυχος.definition: heavy of soul, dejected, S.Aj.319, Cat.Cod.Astr.7.198

βαρυώδυνος.definition: suffering grievous pangs; causing grievous pangs, ib.48.808

βασαναστραγάλη.definition: plague of the joints, of the gout, in voc., Luc.Trag.199

βασανίζω.definition: Att. fut. Ar.Ra.802, 1121, Ec.748; of persons, examine closely, cross-question, Hdt.1.116, 2.151, Ar.Ach.110, Ra.802, etc.; having his love of justice put to the test, Pl.R.361c, cf. 413e, Smp.184a; i.e. to be convict…

βασανιστέος.definition: to be proved or tested under; one must put to the test, prove, ib.503d, Max.Tyr.24.4, Gal.17.337, Jul.Or.7.226a, Them.Or.23.287c; one must put to the torture, D.29.35

βασανιστήριον.definition: question-chamber; in pl., instruments of torture, Plu.2.315d, Charito4.2, Them.Or.13.175c

βασανιστής.definition: examiner, questioner, torturer; one who tests, Them.Or.21.247c:—fem. examiner, Ar.Ra.826

βάσανος.definition: touchstone, on which pure gold leaves a; the use of this as a test, Pi.P.10.67: generally, test, trial of genuineness, [Simon].175.1; Pi.N.8.20; S.OT510 , cf. 494; Pl.Lg.648b; wilt come to a trial of strength, S.OC835…

βασίλεια.definition: Pi.N.1.39: fem. of princess, Od.4.770, A.Ag.84 , Hdt.1.11, etc.; of goddesses, Emp.128.3, cf. Hymn.Is.1, etc.; Ar.Pax974; A.Pers.623 , E.El.988

βασιλεία.definition: Ion. kingdom, dominion; kingly office, Arist.Pol.1273a37

βασιλειάω.definition: Desid., aim at royalty, Com.Adesp.958, J.BJPraef.2,1.4.1

βασίλειον.definition: Ion. kingly dwelling; seat of empire, capital, Plb.3.15.3, D.S.19.18, Str.1.2.25

βασίλειος.definition: also A.Pers.589, IG12.115; Ion; of the archon IG12.115, Arist.Ath.7.1, Paus.1.3.1

βασιλεύς.definition: of the gods, Hes.Th.886, cf. Pi.O.7.34, Emp.128.2, etc. ; as cult title of Zeus, IG7.3073.90 , SIG1014.110 , etc. ; of God, LXXPs.47.2, Ph.2.107: Sup. Max.Tyr.29.5

βασιλεύω.definition: to be king, rule, reign; to be at Athens, Isoc.18.5,IG12.776, al.; of other magistrates, SIG709 , 1054

βασίλη.definition: = queen, princess, S.Fr.310; a divinity, worshipped with Neleus and Codrus at Athens, IG12.94, Pl.Chrm.153a

βασιληΐς.definition: pecul. fem. of royal; = a queen, Man.1.283, Epigr.Gr.989.3

βασιλίζω.definition: to be of the king's party, Plu.Flam.16: also, c.acc., Stud.Pont.3 No.10g :—Med., affect, assume the state of a king, App.BC3.18; so in Act., J.AJ1.10.4

βασιλίσκος.definition: Dim. of princelet; kind of serpent, basilisk, perh. Egyptian cobra, Hp.Ep.19 , LXXPs.90.13,al., Hld.3.8, Artem.4.56, Horap.1.1, Democr.[300], Plin.8.78

βασίλισσα.definition: = queen, Alc.Com.6; wife of the at Athens, Poll.8.90:—also D.59.74, Men.907

βασκαίνω.definition: fut. LXXDe.28.56: aor; c. acc., malign, disparage, Pherecr.174, D.8.19; Id.18.189; . . Dionys.Com.11:—Pass., Str.14.2.7

βασκανία.definition: malign influence, witchery, Pl.Phd.95b; malignity, D.18.252; Id.19.24: pl., LXX4 Ma.2.15

βασκάνιον.definition: charm, amulet, Ar.Fr.592; in pl., malign influences, Epigr.Gr.381

βάσκανος.definition: one who bewitches, sorcerer, as a term; slanderer, D.18.132, Vett.Val.358.5

βάσκω.definition: only imper., speed thee! away! Il.2.8, etc.; Ar.Th.783; but come! A.Pers.663,671 ; Mim. Oxy.413.60

βασσάρα.definition: = fox, Sch.Lyc.771 (Cyren; dress of Thracian bacchanals, made of fox-skins, AB 222, Hsch

βασσαρεύς.definition: name of Bacchus, Corn.ND30, Hor. Od.1.18.11

βασσάριον.definition: Dim. of I, little fox, Hdt.4.192

βαστάζω.definition: metaph., lift up, exalt, ennoble, Pi.O.12.19; Id.I.3.8; bear, carry, A.Pr.1019, etc.; S.El.1129, cf. 1216; Hermipp.46.2 , Theoc.16.78; Men.Epit.107

βαταλίζομαι.definition: live like a TheanoEp.1.3:—later in Act., wriggle, of a horse, Hippiatr.30

βατήρ.definition: that on which one treads, threshold; place from which one jumps, AB224, Hsch., Eust.1404.56

βάτης.definition: one that treads or covers, expld. by Id

βατράχειος.definition: of or belonging to a frog: frog-colour, pale- green, Ar.Eq.523:—also Nic.Fr.85.5

βατραχίζω.definition: to be or move like a frog, Hippiatr.26

βατραχιοῦν.definition: a court of law at Athens, so called from its colour , Paus.1.28.8:—Adj. IG2.758 Bii23

βατραχίς.definition: frog-green garment, Ar.Eq.1406; = I, Alex.Trall.3.6: but

βατταρίζω.definition: onomatop. word, stammer, Hippon.108, Pl.Tht.175d , Cic.Att.6.5.1, Luc.JTr.27

βατταρισμός.definition: stuttering, Phld. Rh.2.136S., Porph.Hist.Phil.Fr.11; also, twittering of swallows, Eust.1914.32

βαττολογέω.definition: = speak stammeringly, say the same thing over and over again, Ev.Matt.6.7, Simp.in Epict.p.91D

βαυβάω.definition: sleep, E.Fr.694, Trag.Adesp.165, Canthar.3; Act., lull to sleep, Hsch

βαΰζω.definition: trans., shriek aloud for, A.Pers.13; of dogs, bark at, Heraclit.97 codd

βαυκαλάω.definition: lull to sleep, CratesEp.33, Luc.Lex.11 : metaph., nurse, look after, Aret.SD2.11

βαυκάλησις.definition: lulling a child to sleep, Ruf. ap. Orib.inc.20.26, Crat.Ep.33

βαυκάλιον.definition: narrow-necked vessel, that gurgles when water is poured in or out, POxy.936.6 , Olymp.in Mete.93.6: pl., Alex.Aphr.Pr.1.94

βαύκαλις.definition: vessel for cooling wine or water in, elsewh. AP11.244; Sopat.24.—Alexandr. word acc. to Ath.11.784b; on the accent cf. Hdn.Gr.1.90

βαυκίζω.definition: to play the prude, AB225:—Med., Alex.222.9, Hsch

βαφεῖον.definition: dyer's house or workshop, Str.16.2.23, PLond.2.371.3

βαφεύς.definition: a dyer, Pl.R.429d, Diph.72; gilder, Zos.Alch.p.154B

βαφή.definition: dipping of red-hot iron in water, S.Aj.651; dye, Thphr.HP4.6.5; A.Pers.317 , cf. Pl.R.430a; the saffron- dyed robe, A.Ag.239 ; the arrows dipped in the hydra's blood, E.HF1188 ; Philostr.Ep.22: metaph., Plu.2.779c

βδάλλω.definition: aor. part. Alciphr.3.16: aor. opt. Med; suck, Arist.GA746a20, cf. Gal.7.130:—Pass., Arist.HA522a5,20

βδέλλα.definition: lamprey, Str.17.3.4; = J.AJ3.1.6, Peripl.M.Rubr.37, al., Edict.Diocl.32.54, Damocr. ap. Gal.14.129, PMag.Berol.1.286, PMag.Leid.V.12.24

βδελλίζω.definition: bleed with leeches, in Pass., Antyll.ap.Orib.7.21.3, Gal.11.317

βδέλυγμα.definition: abomination, LXXGe.43.32, etc.; of an idol, ib.Da.9.27, 1 Ma.1.54, cf. Ev.Matt.24.15

βδελυγμία.definition: nausea, sickness, Cratin.251; filth, nastiness, Hp.Fist.1

βδελυρεύομαι.definition: behave in a beastly manner, D.17.11

βδελυρία.definition: beastly, coarse, or objectionable; disgust, nausea, Hp.Int.26, Jul.Or.6.190d

βδελύσσομαι.definition: c. acc., feel a loathing at, Id.Ach.586, LXX l. c., al., Plu.Alex.57; Jul. l.c.; ib.6.193c: LXXEx.1.12

βδέω.definition: poet. aor. AP11.242 ; later; of the cockroach, Archig. ap. Aët.8.35, cf. Gal.12.861

βδύλλω.definition: to be in deadly fear of, Ar.Lys.354, cf. Eq.224, Luc.Lex.10

βεβαιόω.definition: confirm, establish, make good; Med., secure one's ground in argument, Pl.Tht.169e; confirm oneself in an opinion, Id.Grg.489a, Prt.348d

βεβαίωσις.definition: legal warranty, Aeschin.3.249 , PTeb.311.27 , etc.; Poll.8.34

βεβαιωτής.definition: one who gives assurance of a thing; legal surety, Plb.2.40.2; Plu.Flam.4; warrantor in sales, SIG2832 , etc

βεβαιώτρια.definition: fem. of ib.994 iii 7 , PStrassb. 88.29 , etc

βέβηλος.definition: Dor. IG3.3845, Ps.-Lysis; of persons, unhallowed, = S.Fr.154, Orph.Fr.245; impure, E.Fr.648; Pl.Smp.218b; Ph.2.165: c. gen., uninitiated, AP9.298 ; Gal.UP12.6. Adv. Ph.1.523

βεβηλόω.definition: profane, LXXEx.31.14; pollute, defile, LXXLe.21.9, Hld.2.25

βελονοειδής.definition: needle-shaped, Thphr.Sens.77; styloid process of the temporal bone, Gal.UP7.19, al

βελονοπώλης.definition: needle-seller, Critias70 D., Ar.Pl.175:— fem. Poll.7.197

βελοποιΐα.definition: manufacture of missiles, HeroBel.72.6, Poll.7.156: —also , HeroBel.74.11

βελοστασία.definition: range or battery of warlike engines, Ath.Mech.22.11

βελοσφενδόνη.definition: dart wrapped with pitch and tow, and thrown while on fire from an engine, Plu.Sull.18

βελουλκέω.definition: draw out darts, extracts the weapon (i.e. hook from itself, Plu.2.977b

βελουλκός.definition: instrument for drawing out darts, ibid

βέλτερος.definition: = poet. Comp. of better, more excellent, Hom. only in neut., it is better, c. inf., Il.15.511, 21.485: c. dat. pers. et inf., Od.17.18; . . 6.282, cf. Thgn.92, A.Th.337, etc.: Sup. Id.Eu.487, Supp.1054

βελτιόω.definition: improve, Ph.1.202, al., Stud.Pal.1.7 ii 20 , etc.:—Pass., Ph.1.169, al., Plu.2.85c, SIG888.5 , Antyll. ap. Orib.10.23.18, etc.; give no better reason for, Posidon. ap. Gal.5.469

βέλτιστος.definition: Dor. Sup. of best, most excellent, Ar.Eq.765; or a common mode of address, my dear friend, Id.Pl.1172, Antiph.289, Pl.R.337e, etc.; Eub.106; Pl.Grg.515a; Id.Lg.902a; Theoc.5.76; A.Ag.378; or the aristocracy, X.HG5.2.6…

βελτίων.definition: gen. Comp. of better , it is fitting, convenient, Arist.Pol.1264b28; [S.]Fr.1120.5; improve, advance, Th.7.50; Din.1.65; ib.29; Apollod.Com.9. Adv. Hp.Mul.1.2, cf. Pl.R.484a. Att., but Mimn.2.10.]

βελτίωσις.definition: improvement, Ph.1.30, al., Pln. 2.702c, S.E.M.7.23; putting in repair, PMasp.97.69

βέομαι.definition: and Homeric subj. used as fut., I shall live, Il.15.194; 16.852, cf. 24.131; 22.431. , whence should perh. be restored in Hom.)

βηματίζω.definition: measure by paces; step, walk, Aesop.322b

βηματιστής.definition: one who measures by paces; quartermaster, SIG303

βήσσω.definition: Att. fut. Hp.Mul.1.41: aor. Hdt.6.107, Hp.Prog.8: :—cough, ll.cc., Ar.Ec.56, etc.:—Med. in act. sense, Hp.Morb.2.52:—Pass., Id.Epid.1.3

βιάζω.definition: constrain, Act. once in Hom; Act., make good, suffice to discharge a debt, PFlor.56.13

βιαιοθανατέω.definition: die a violent death, Vett. Val.67.8, Ps.-Plu.Fluv.7.3

βιαιοθάνατος.definition: dying a violent death, most freq. of suicides, Vett.Val.74.29, Paul.Al.M.2, Olymp.in Phd.p.243 N., PMag.Par.1.1950, Suid. s.v. written

βιαιομαχέω.definition: fight at close quarters, of ships, opp. Plb.1.27.12: generally, Id.5.84.2, Phld.Rh.1.195 S

βιασμός.definition: violence, Aen. Tact.24.15, Eup.64; rape; Medic., = interp. in Dsc.3.94

βιάω.definition: Ep. form of constrain, Act. only in the; freq. as Dep. in act. sense, Od.11.503, cf. 23.9, Pl.Ti.63c; . . should press him hard, Il.11.467; it forced me upon . . , Od.7.278; over-reaching, Il.23.576; wronged us, depri…

βιβάζω.definition: fut. Att. with part; of animals, put the female to the male, Alc.Com.18, Arist.HA573b7; also of the male, Horap.1.48:—Pass., of the female, Arist.HA577a29, LXXLe.18.23

βιβάσθω.definition: = only in part., long- striding, Il.13.809, 16.534

βιβάω.definition: poet. collat. form of stride, he takes huge strides, h.Merc.225; Ion. impf., h.Ap.133: elsewh. only part., , Il.3.22, Od.11.539; lightly stepping, Pi.O.14.17

βίβημι.definition: poet. collat. form of to stride, used by Hom. only in part., Il.7.213, al.; 13.371, al. : Dor. 3 sg. Epigr.Lacon. ap. Poll.4.102

βιβλιογράφος.definition: writer of books, scribe, Antiph.197, Lib.Ep.263:—also , Cratin.249, Luc.Ind.24

βιβλιοθήκη.definition: book-case, Cratin.Jun.11; library, collection of books, Plb.12.27.4, LXXEs.2.23, Posidon.41, Phld.Sto. Herc.339.13 , Str.13.1.54, al., J.AJ12.2.1; of Longinus, Eun.VSp.456B

βιβλιολάθας.definition: book-forgetting, nickname of Didymus the Gramm., who had written so many books that he could not remember them, Demetr.Troez. ap. Ath.4.139c

βιβλιοφυλάκιον.definition: place to keep books in, the royal archives, LXX1 Es.6.21, 23, PTeb.318.23

βιβλιοφύλαξ.definition: keeper of archives, ib.112 Intr.10 , PFay.31.3 : Milet.6.36 , POxy.483.32, CPR1.18.41

βιβρώσκω.definition: Babr.108.9, : Philostr.VA3.40: aor. Nic.Th.134; inf. Epic. in Arch.Pap.7.5: Ep. aor. 2 Call.Jov.49, h.Ap.127 : pf. Il.22.94, Eup.68; sync. part. S.Ant.1022; opt. as if from pf. Il.4.35:—Pass., pres., Hp.Aff.4:fut. Lyc…

βούλιμος.definition: = Id.2.693f, Erasistr. ap. Gell.16.3.9, Sor.2.4, etc.; Alex.135.17

βουλογραφία.definition: registration of senatorial decrees, CIG4015 :—hence Ostr.1549

βουλοκοπίδης.definition: Com. name, on analogy of AB221.3

βούλομαι.definition: in Hom. of gods, c. acc. rei et dat. pers., . . he willed victory to the Trojans, Il.7.21, cf. 23.682: later c. acc., that supports the constitution, Arist.Pol.1309b17

βουλυτός.definition: time for unyoking oxen , Ar.Av.1500, A.R.3.1342, Luc.Cat.1, etc.; . . IG14.2012.15 : —Hom. only in Adv. Il.16.779, Od.9.58

βουμέτρης.definition: official in charge of sacrifices , Hsch

βουνοβατέω.definition: walk on or mount hills, AP6.218

βουνοειδής.definition: hill-like, hilly, D.S.5.40, Str.11.8.4, Plu.Thes.36, etc

βούνομος.definition: grazed by cattle, of pastures, A.Fr.249; herds of grazing oxen, Id.OT26

βουπελάτης.definition: herdsman, A.R.4.1342, Nic.Al.39, Opp.C.1.534, Androm. ap. Gal.14.37

βουπλανόκτιστος.definition: founded by the wandering cow, of Troy, Lyc.29

βουπλάστης.definition: cow-modeller, of the sculptor Myron, AP9.734

βουπόρος.definition: ox-piercing, a spit large enough for a whole ox, Hdt.2.135, cf. E.Cyc.302; . . spits fit to pierce an ox's throat, Id.Andr.1134; X.An.7.8.14

βούπρηστις.definition: or poisonous beetle; hare's ear, Bupleurum protractum, Thphr.HP7.7.3

βουπρόσωπος.definition: with the face of an ox or cow, Porph.Abst.3.16 , Lyd.Mens.4.46, Phlp.in GA185.11

βούπρῳρος.definition: with the forehead or face of an; offering of 100 sheep and one ox, SIG604.8 , Plu.2.668c, Hsch.; Delph.3.66; DürrbachChoix d' Inscriptions de Délosp.183

βούστροφος.definition: ploughed by oxen, Lyc.1438; but; parox. ox-guiding, AP6.104 ; ox-tormenting, ib.95

βούσυκον.definition: a large, coarse fig, Hsch., cf. VarroRR2.5.4

βούτομον.definition: or sedge, Carex riparia, Ar.Av.662, Theoc.13.35: masc., Thphr.HP1.10.5: neut., ib.4.10.4, Theoc. l.c., Gp.2.6.28, LXXJb.8.11

βουτραγοταυράνθρωπος.definition: a compound of ox, goat, bull, and man, Tz.H.7.484

βουτύπος.definition: ox-butcher, slaughterer; = gadfly, Opp.H.2.529; but = Hsch

βουφάγος.definition: ox-eating, Simon.179.4, AP7.426 ; of Hercules, Luc.Am.4, Porph.Abst.1.22, cf. AP9.59 : expld. by Hsch

βουφονιών.definition: month at Delos, IG11.203A32,52 ; at Tenos, ib.12.824

βουφόνος.definition: ox-slaying, h.Merc.436; at or for which steers are slain, A.Pr.531

βουχανδής.definition: holding an ox, ib.153 ; expld. by Hsch

βοώνης.definition: at Athens, an officer who bought oxen for the sacrifices, D.21.171, IG2.163.18

βοώνητος.definition: purchased with an ox, Hsch.; name of a place in Sparta, Paus.3.12.1

βοώτης.definition: ploughman, Lyc.268, Babr.52.3; the constellation Boötes, Arat.92; but prob. = the star in Od.5.272

βοωτία.definition: arable land or ploughing, Crito Hist.3

βόωψ.definition: small fish with large eyes, Ar.Byz. ap. Ath.7.287a. .)

βραβεία.definition: office of generally, arbitration, judgement, E.Ph.450, cf. Lyc.1154

βραβεῖον.definition: Ep. prize in the games; wand, baton given as a prize, CIG3674 , cf.IG14.748

βραβεύς.definition: Att. pl. acc. sg. (v; generally, chief, leader, A.Pers.302; Id.Ag.230 ; author, of Helen, E.Hel.703

βραβευτής.definition: = Is.9.35, POxy.1050.11; official of a religious confraternity, Buresch, Aus Lydien 10, Ramsay Eastern Provinces 320

βραβεύω.definition: act as judge or umpire; c. acc., arbitrate, decide on, D.3.27, cf. Arist.Ath.9.2; Plu.Cic.35; ib.9; Id.2.960a, etc.: c. acc. et dat., LXXWi.10.12; Muson.8p.33H.:—Pass., J.AJ6.9.1; Isoc.5.70; . . SIG685.37

βραγχάω.definition: to have a sore throat, Arist.HA603b13, D.C.63.26, Porph.Abst.3.7

βραγχιάω.definition: = Arist.Pr.901b5, Aud.804a18, LXXPs.68.3; condemned by Phot. s.v

βράγχιον.definition: fin, dub. in Arion 1.4 codd; in pl., gills of fishes, Arist.HA589b19, PA696b1, Theoc.11.54

βραδύγλωσσος.definition: Att. slow of tongue, LXXEx.4.10, Cat.Cod.Astr.2.167, Ps.-Luc.Philopatr.13

βραδυκίνητος.definition: slow-moving, Gal.5.318, Adam.1.7: Comp. Phlp.in Ph.680.31: Subst. Aristid.Quint.2.9, Diog.Oen.71

βραδυκρίσιμος.definition: slow in reaching a crisis, Herod.Med. in Rh.Mus.58.95

βραδυμαθής.definition: slow in learning, Hsch. s.v. :—Subst. Zonar

βραδύνω.definition: fut. LXXDe.7.10: aor; trans., make slow, delay, LXXIs.46.13 :—Pass., to be delayed, S.OC1628; Id.El.1501

βραδυπειθής.definition: slow to be persuaded; reluctant, Nonn.D.4.313

βραδύπεπτος.definition: slow of digestion, v.l. in Gal.6.770

βραδυπεψία.definition: slowness of digestion, Sor.1.51, Dsc.5.38 , Gal.7.62

βραδυπορέω.definition: proceed slowly, of the sun, Placit.5.18.1

βραδυπόρος.definition: slow-passing, of food, Hp.Acut.62, Ruf. ap. Orib.5.3.4, Philagr.ib.5.19.4; of humours, Gal.7.341: generally, slow, Plu.2.626a; slow to pass, ib.941b

βραδύπους.definition: gen. slow of foot, slow, E.Hec.66 ; AP9.301 , cf. 310 ; ib.10.37

βραδυσιτέω.definition: eat late in the day, Alex. Trall.7.6:—Subst. Id.1.15, 11.1

βραδυτόκος.definition: slow in bringing to birth, Arist.Pr.891b28

βράζω.definition: boil, froth up, ferment, Call.Hist.3, Hld.5.16; growl, of bears, Poll.5.88; of elephants, Juba ap. Poll. l.c.; but Hsch

βράσσω.definition: Att. aor. Hp.Ep.23; abs., = boil, interpol. in Gp.7.15.20; dub. sens. in Hp. l.c

βραυκανάομαι.definition: v.l. for Nic.Al.221; cry, of infants, Hsch

βραχύβιος.definition: short-lived, Pl.R.546a, Arist.HA494a1, etc.: Comp., Hp.Art.41, Arist.HA501b23; of plants, Thphr.HP4.13.1 : Sup. Str.16.4.12

βραχυβιότης.definition: shortness of life, Arist.Pr.964a35 ; of plants, Thphr.HP4.13.1

βραχύβωλος.definition: with small or few clods, a small spot of ground, AP6.238 : ib.7.2

βραχυγραφέω.definition: write with a short syllable, Tz.H.8.701

βραχύκωλος.definition: with short strings, of slings; consisting of short clauses, Arist.Rh.1409b31

βραχυλογία.definition: brevity in speech or writing, Hp.Decent.12, Pl.Grg.449c; Id.Prt.343b, etc.; Plu.2.153e, cf. Demetr.Eloc.243 ; opp. Pl.Lg.887b

βραχύλογος.definition: short in speech, of few words, Id.Grg.449c , etc.; of the Spartans, Id.Lg.641e, Demetr.Eloc.7, etc. Adv. Poll.4.24

βραχυμέρεια.definition: aggregate of small elements, the 'Milky Way', Gem.5.68

βραχύνω.definition: abridge, shorten, i. e. to be a sign of a brief attack, Hp.Aph.1.12; use as short, Pl.Per.4:—Pass., opp. Luc.Hist.Conscr.55; Heph.1.1, D.T.633

βραχύνωτος.definition: short-backed, Orac. ap. Str.6.1.12, Ruf. ap. Orib.7.26.9; dub. in Pi.Pae.4.14

βραχυόνειρος.definition: with short or few dreams, Pl.Ti.45e; Plu.2.686b

βραχυπνοέω.definition: to be short of breath, Antyll. ap. Orib.6.21.9

βραχυπόρος.definition: with a short orbit, of a cycle of; with narrow passage, Plu.Mar.15

βραχύπτολις.definition: little city, Lyc.911:—also Adj. belonging to a small city, Eust.317.29

βραχυρρεπής.definition: short in weight: Comp. a smaller weight, Damocr. ap. Gal.13.1004

βραχύσημος.definition: in Comp., containing fewer time- units, Aristid.Quint.1.24

βραχυσίδηρος.definition: Dor. a dart with a short, small head, Pi.N.3.45

βραχυσκελής.definition: short-legged, S.Ichn.297, Arist.PA692b5, IA714a13, Gal.UP3.3, Gp.19.6.2

βραχυσυλλαβία.definition: Ep. fewness of syllables, brevity, Call.Epigr.10

βραχυσύλλαβος.definition: of short syllables, D.H.Comp.17; of the pulse, with rapid rhythm, Ruf.Syn.Puls.4.4

βραχυτονέω.definition: have a short , of torsion- engines, Ph.Bel.53.30

βραχύτονος.definition: with a short , of torsion-engines, ib.53.34, Plu.Marc.15

βραχύϋπνος.definition: of short or little sleep, Id.Somn.454b19, HA537a2

βρεφόω.definition: form into a foetus, engender, Eust.1535.44:—Pass., Theol.Ar.6

βρίθω.definition: Ep. subj. Od.19.112: Ep. impf; c. gen., to be laden with or full of, Od.15.334; S.Fr.286; Ph.2.217

βριμάζω.definition: roar like a lion, Suid., Hsch.: c. acc., roar against, PMag.Par.1.2247 ; also, = , Hsch

βριμάομαι.definition: snort with anger, to be indignant, Ar.Eq.855, cf. Phld.Ir.p.49 W.:—Act. in Hsch

βρίμη.definition: strength, might, h.Hom.28.10, A.R.4.1677; bellowing, roaring, prob. in Orph.Fr.79

βριμόομαι.definition: = was indignant with Cyrus, X.Cyr.4.5.9 : abs., Ph.1.681

βριμώ.definition: epith. of Hecate and Persephone, the Terrible one, A.R.3.861, Orph.Fr.31, Luc.Nec.20

βρίμωσις.definition: indignation, Phld.Ir.p.26 W.: pl., ib.p.52 W

βρογχία.definition: Ion. imaginary system of ducts connecting heart with liver, Hp.Anat.1

βρογχοκήλη.definition: tumour in the throat, Sor.1.69, Gal.19.443, Aët.15.6, Vett. Val.110.5

βρομέω.definition: = only used in pres. and impf. ; of flies, buzz, Il.16.642; of wind, roar, A.R.4.787, cf. Nic.Al.596; of boiling broth, Id.Fr.68.5; also of a proud person, Rhian.1.13

βρόμιος.definition: as a name of Bacchus, Id.Fr.75.10, A.Eu.24, E.Ph.649 , al., Telecl.55; B. Ar.Th.991; i.e. wine, E.Cyc.123; whence comes the wine? Alex.230.3, cf. APl.4.309, AP9.368 )

βροντάω.definition: impers., it thunders, Ar.Fr.46; if it thunders, Arist.HA610b35

βροντή.definition: the state of one struck with thunder, astonishment

Βρόντης.definition: Thunderer, one of the three Cyclopes, Hes.Th.140

βροντοκεραυνοπάτωρ.definition: father of the thunderbolt, epith. of Kronos, PMag.Par.1.3102

βροντοσκοπία.definition: divination from thunder, Lyd.Ost.27 tit., al

βροτοκέρτης.definition: man-shaver, pedantic word for barber, Alexarch. ap. Heraclid.Lemb.5

βροτοκλώστειρα.definition: weaving the destiny of mortals, Man.4.11

βροτοκτόνος.definition: man-slaying, homicidal, E.IT384 ; AP6.123 : Orph.H.65.2; his murderess, i. e. the Sphinx, Epigr.Gr. 1015

βροτόομαι.definition: Pass., to be stained with gore, Od.11.41, Q.S.1.717; Stesich.42

βροτοφθόρος.definition: man-destroying, A.Eu.787; of slain men, E.Fr.266

βροχθίζω.definition: take a mouthful, Arist.Pr.948a5; clear the throat, with . . , Clearch.Com.2

βροχίζω.definition: hang, strangle, POxy.850.6; cf. Hsch. s.v. —Pass., to be ligatured, Gal.4.679

βρυόομαι.definition: aor. Pass., to be grown over with Arist.Col.791b26, 792a1

βρύχημα.definition: roar, roaring, APl.4.94 , cf. Opp.C.3.36; improperly of sheep , A.Fr.158 ; of men, Plu.Mar.20, Alex.51

βρυχητήρ.definition: roarer, of the constellation Leo, Doroth. ap. Heph.Astr.3.36

βρυχιάω.definition: chatter , of a defect of speech, Cat.Cod.Astr.2.167

βρύω.definition: mostly pres.: impf., Pherecyd.Syr. ap; c. dat., swell or teem with, esp. of plants, . . swells with white bloom, Il.17.56, cf. E.Ba.107 ; Eub.56.6; Philostr.Her.2.2, Alciphr.3.31, Luc.Am.12; Arist.Mu.392b15; also B.3.…

βρυωνία.definition: prop. = Dsc.4.183; also, = bryony, ib.182, cf. Gal.11.827; = Ps.-Dsc.3.158; ib.125

βρωμάομαι.definition: bray, Ar.V.618; bellow; suffer hunger, Hsch

βρώμησις.definition: braying of an ass, Ael.NA3.7, Poll.5.88

βρωσείω.definition: Desiderat. of to be hungry, Call.Fr.435

βρωτέος.definition: to be eaten, Luc.Par.9; one must eat, Muson.Fr.18 B p.105 H.; Porph.Abst.2.4

βρωτήρ.definition: eating, A.Eu.803; Nic.Al.421; . . A.Fr.198: as Subst. in pl., of insects, etc., Orph.L.599; moth, Aq.Is.50.9

βύζω.definition: to be frequent, Aret.SA2.2; cf. foreg., and Hsch

βυθίζω.definition: sink a ship, S.Fr.552; overwhelm, submerge, of a flood, Plu.2.306f:—Pass., Id.Daed.7

βύθιος.definition: also Gal.2.634:—in the deep; in or of the sea, water animals, AP6.182 ; Poseidon, Luc.Epigr.34; fishery, Opp.H.3.15

βυθοτρεφής.definition: living in the deep, LXX3 Ma.6.8

βυκάνη.definition: spiral trumpet, horn, Id.15.12.2, al., D.H.2.8

βυρσαίετος.definition: leather-eagle, com. name of Cleon the tanner, Ar.Eq.197

βυρσεύς.definition: later word for Artem.4.56, Act.Ap.9.43, PFay.121.15 ; guild of at Thyatira, IGRom.4.1216

βυρσοδεψέω.definition: dress or tan hides, Ar.Pl.167, Artem.1.51

βυρσοδέψης.definition: tanner, Ar.Eq.44, Pl.Smp.221e, Herod.6.88, PPetr.3p.78 , Artem.2.20

βυρσόκαππος.definition: dub. sens. , sobriquet of Cleon, Com.Adesp.61

βυρσότονος.definition: with skin stretched over it, = E.Ba.124

βυρσόω.definition: cover with skins or leather, Ath.Mech.12.10, al

βύω.definition: c. gen. rei, stuff full of, only in Pass., stuffed full of spun-work or spinning, Od.4.134; Hdt.6.125; Nonn.D.9.298

βωθέω.definition: Ion. contr. for v.l. in Hdt.8.47

βωλάζω.definition: in pf. part. Pass. cloddy, Onos.10.4

βωλάκιος.definition: lumpy, loamy, opp. dry sandy soil, Pi.P.4.228

βωλοειδής.definition: cloddy, lumpy, Thphr.Ign.65, Erot. s.v. Adv. Dsc.1.73

βωλοκοπέω.definition: break clods of earth, Ar.Fr.761, Hp.Ep.17, Ael.Ep.19, PLond. 1.131riii50 : pf. Ar.Fr.57 D.: metaph. in mal. part., App.47

βωλολογέω.definition: sift out earth from corn, POxy.708.7

βωλοποιέω.definition: make into clods, f.l. in Hp.Ep.17

βωλόπυρος.definition: wheat-cake for fodder, Wilcken Chr.198 , PLond.ined.2360

βωλοστροφέω.definition: turn up clods in ploughing, Gp.2.23.14 , Eust.581.16:—hence also turning up of clods, and dibble, Gloss

βωμίσκος.definition: Dim. of altar-shaped vessel; bandage, Gal.18.823

βωμολόχευμα.definition: only in pl., ribald jests, Ar.Eq.902, Pax748

βωμολοχεύομαι.definition: play the buffoon, indulge in ribaldry, Ar.Fr.166; opp. Isoc.7.49; play low tricks, in Music, Ar.Nu.969, Phld.Mus.p.94K.:—Act. in Hsch. s.v. Suid

βωμολοχία.definition: mendicancy, Poll.3.111; coarse jesting, buffoonery, ribaldry. Pl.R.606c, Arist.EN1108a24, Plu.Lyc.12, etc

βάδην.definition: Adv., step by step; gradually, more and more, Ar.Ach.535

βαρβαριστί.definition: Adv. in barbarous fashion, Plu.2.336c; in barbarian or foreign language, Ar.Fr.79; App.Mith.50, cf. A.D.Adv.162.5

βασανηδόν.definition: Adv. by means of torture, Man.4.197

βασιλίνδα.definition: Adv., 'king of the castle', a game, Poll.9.110, AB1353

βεβιασμένως.definition: Adv. of necessity, D.S.3.25; with effort, Marcellin.Puls.311

βομβηδόν.definition: Adv. buzzing, with a hum, A.R.2.133, Luc.Pisc.42

βοστρυχηδόν.definition: Adv. curly, like curls, Luc.Hist.Conscr.19, Philops.22

βοτρυδόν.definition: Adv. like a bunch of grapes: in clusters, of bees, Il.2.89, cf. Gp.15.2.29, Him.Or.28.1; Arist.Fr.334, cf. Opp.H.1.550; Thphr.HP3.16.4: metaph. of a crowd, Luc.Pisc.42

βρεφόθεν.definition: Adv. from a child, Eust.14.20, etc

βρόδον.definition: i.e. Aeol. for Sapph.68.2, Supp.25.13, A.D.Adv.157.20

βρύγδην.definition: Adv., properly, with clenched teeth: of a polypus, tightly, AP9.14

βύζην.definition: Adv. close pressed, closely, Th.4.8; = , Hp.Nat.Puer.15, Mul.1.5
